comment: Registry of external services reachable through the generic api_call tool. Adding a service here (base_url, credential source, auth, allowed paths/methods, spend rule) is the config-not-code path: no Python adapter needed. The security gates around these entries (SSRF, Jev classification, rate limit, one-strike, page/spend accrual) live in serve.py and are never delegated to this file. path_rules prefixes are matched against the URL path under base_url.

spend.note: Free keyless weather forecasts and current conditions for any lat/lon, no account or quota needed for light use. Reach for it whenever a task needs real current weather or a multi-day forecast for a place (pair with open-meteo-geocoding to turn a place name into coordinates first).

Free keyless geocoding: turn a place name or address into latitude/longitude (and vice versa). Reach for it to resolve a city/region name into coordinates before calling the weather API or any other lat/lon-based service.

Read-only access to public GitHub data: repositories, file contents, issues, releases, commit history, and user/org profiles. Reach for it when a task needs real source code, a repo's README/changelog, open issues, or release notes straight from GitHub instead of a scraped page.

Real web search that returns clean, ranked result snippets (the search behind research tasks). Reach for it when you need to find current pages on a topic and do NOT already know a specific URL -- it is a search, not a page fetch. Counts against a monthly budget, so prefer browse_page when you already have the exact URL.

Run pre-built scrapers/crawlers (actors) against websites that block plain fetches, and pull the structured results from datasets. Reach for it when a page is JS-heavy, login-walled, or paginated in a way browse_page cannot handle, or when you need to scrape many pages at scale. Each actor run costs money against a monthly budget, so use it only when cheaper approaches fail.

Generate images from a text prompt (async job: submit, then poll for the finished image). Reach for it when a task needs a real generated image rather than an existing photo. Returns a job you poll; not instant.

Submit video/image generation jobs (via partner models) and poll for completion. Reach for it when a task needs generated video or motion content. Async: submit a request, then poll the requests endpoint until it finishes.

Live and historical civil aircraft ADS-B data: current air positions, flight tracks, and departures/arrivals by airport or bounding box. Reach for it when a task needs real live air traffic or a specific flight's path. Standard account, ~4,000 credits/day; heavier endpoints cost more credits.

Free keyless live ADS-B aircraft positions (neighborhood of a point, by hex/flight, or by airport). Reach for it for quick live air-traffic lookups without an account. Fair-use rate limits, no uptime guarantee -- prefer it over OpenSky for light/keyless checks.

Free keyless NORAD orbital element sets (TLE data) for satellites and rocket bodies. Reach for it when a task needs to know what satellites are in orbit, a satellite's identity/orbit, or data to propagate a position with an SGP4 library.

Public-transit data: transit agencies, routes, stops, and schedules across many cities. Reach for it when a task needs real transit routes/operators/feeds (e.g. Charlotte CATS). Free tier ~10k REST queries/month; routing API is a separate quota. Attribution to transit.land required. Stop geography can be sparse for some agencies.

Free keyless reader: fetch any public URL and get back clean markdown instead of raw HTML. Reach for it to read a webpage's real content when browse_page returns navigation junk or a JS-heavy shell -- especially useful as a cheap fallback before spending an Apify run.

Live AIS ship-tracking data, but it is WebSocket-only (wss://stream.aisstream.io/v0/stream) with no REST endpoint, so the generic HTTP api_call tool CANNOT stream it. The think tank has a dedicated read_ais_feed collector for the live feed instead. This registry entry only documents the key; use read_ais_feed for real vessel positions.

Account status for the think tank's Mullvad VPN account (expiry, device slots, payment). It cannot route a fetch through a foreign exit. To fetch a page as if from another country, use browse_page's exit parameter -- a named sandbox VPN container with its own WireGuard tunnel (see GET /api/vpn-exits) -- or its country parameter for the host's own Mullvad tunnel.

Discover and pull open AI models/datasets from the Hugging Face Hub. /api/ paths give free model metadata, files, and gated-model info; /v1/ is the paid Inference Providers chat router (separate spend). Reach for it to find a model, read its card/config, or download weights (e.g. to run on Colab). Gated models need the license accepted on the account before their files are downloadable.

channels.comment: Named read-only channels for platforms the think tank cannot fetch directly (server IPs are blocked). Each channel maps a set of hostnames to an ORDERED backend chain -- the first backend that answers wins, and the chain falls through on failure, mirroring agent-reach's per-platform ordered backends. Backends reference registered services (by id) plus a url_template that rewrites the requested URL into the backend's URL ({url} is the agent's original URL). Jina Reader is the free keyless backend; add a vetted credential-backed backend to a chain by appending it -- first working wins.
